doc.title: Roy McCurdy interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

title: Five Spot and touring upstate with the Jazz Brothers
summary: Playing the Five Spot in 1959, being strictly into jazz, and touring upstate with Garrison and Davis on bass.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Rock ‘n Roll was kind of in its infancy — well it’d been around for a few years, but you were into the jazz.

Yeah. I was strictly into jazz at that time. Yeah. That’s all I wanted to do. I knew that was what I was going to do. I had made up my mind that’s what I was going to do. And well actually that’s how we met Chuck and we just, they, we went on the road and did little © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-

things with the band and traveled around all through the Upstate New York area, in the wintertime too, in the cold trailers. It was incredible. We had a couple of good musicians too that came on the band. Jimmy Garrison played with us for a while, Steve Davis played bass with us for a while. So it was great, it was nice.
When you got through the Jazz Brothers time, other things opened up for you. Betty Carter a few years later?
